stories.title: Replit Missions: agent swarms that work to a goal and a hard budget
stories.plain: Replit launched Missions, where you describe an outcome and a team of AI agents plans, builds, tests and iterates until an independent AI judge says it is met. You set a spending cap and list which actions need your approval first.
stories.eng: Each agent runs in its own isolated cloud environment with dev tools, databases, auth and deploy access; agents work on separate copies and a dedicated agent resolves merge conflicts. Spend is checked at every step and paid services are blocked at the proxy once the cap is hit. A 'Mission agreement' records the success criteria, budget and approval gates.
specs: Up to 19x with 32 agents vs up to 4x single agent
49,000/s vs 9,800/s for a Claude Code build
stories.point: The point: swarms are becoming a product with budgets, approval gates and an external judge built in, not just a research demo.
stories.means: Most multi-agent tools so far either ran a handful of agents or let token costs run away. Missions treats a big task like a contract: define what success looks like, give a budget, and let many agents work in parallel until a separate judge model checks the result against the criteria. If money runs out first, work stops unresolved. Replit's numbers come from its own tests, and it notes the Claude Code comparison used one run per setup, so treat them as indicative rather than independent benchmarks.
stories.industry: Cognition, Factory and now Replit are all shipping 'manager' layers that coordinate many coding agents. The hard part is shifting from getting agents to write code to controlling cost, permissions and verification across dozens of them, which is where vendors are competing.
stories.you: If you try swarm tools, write the success criteria and tests first; the judge is only as good as the spec it checks. Put spending caps and approval gates on anything customer-facing, and enforce them outside the agent (proxy or IAM), as Replit does.
terms: Agent swarm
Many AI agents working in parallel on parts of one goal, coordinated by software or another agent.
AI judge
A separate model that checks finished work against agreed criteria instead of trusting the agent's own report.
stories.why: Replit says it open-sourced a self-hostable version of the monitoring platform its agents built.
stories.source: Replit blog · 17 Nov; The New Stack · 17 Nov

stories.title: Walmart's agent use doubles; it builds a gate for outside agents
stories.plain: Walmart said use of Sparky, its AI shopping assistant, more than doubled in the US last quarter. It is also launching a Walmart Agent Gateway to control how outside AI agents shop on its platform.
stories.eng: The gateway manages approved external agents, with customer-set permissions and spending limits. Sparky added voice and image shopping, new language support, and expanded to Mexico, Canada and Sam's Club.
specs: Walmart Agent Gateway for external agents
stories.point: The point: the largest retailer wants agent shopping, but on its terms, with a checkpoint every outside agent must pass.
stories.means: Shopping agents from OpenAI, Google and others can now browse and buy on a user's behalf. For a retailer that raises questions: who is this agent, what is it allowed to spend, and who is liable if it buys the wrong thing? A gateway is like an API gateway for agents: it authenticates them, applies the customer's permissions and limits, and logs what they do. Walmart's own numbers suggest its first-party agent is growing fast and raising order size.
stories.industry: Agent commerce is splitting into two camps: general assistants that shop anywhere, and retailers that want to own the agent relationship. Gateways like this, and payment standards such as x402, will decide whether third-party agents get smooth access or friction.
stories.you: If you build agents that transact, expect identity, scoped permissions and spending limits to be required by platforms, not optional. Design your agent to present credentials and respect per-user caps from day one.
terms: Agent gateway
A control point that identifies outside AI agents and enforces what they may do and spend.
Basket size
The total value of items in one order.
stories.why: CEO John Furner announced the figures with Walmart's third-quarter fiscal 2027 results.
stories.source: AIM Media House (via Rio Rundown) · 21 Nov

stories.title: Google folds Duplex into Gemini so it can phone businesses for you
stories.plain: Google's Duplex technology, which makes phone calls to businesses on your behalf, is now part of the Tasks feature in the Gemini app. You can ask Gemini to call a place, for example to make a reservation.
stories.eng: Google Research says the system now runs on foundation models and handles low-latency voice conversations with real businesses. Information gathered from these calls (hours, availability) feeds back into Search and Maps.
specs: Tasks feature in the Gemini app
Over 1 trillion times in Search and Maps
Yossi Matias, Yaniv Leviathan, Janet Zhou
stories.point: The point: agents are moving off the screen and into the phone line, acting in the parts of the world that have no API.
stories.means: Duplex was first shown in 2018 as a scripted system that could book a haircut by phone. Rebuilding it on foundation models means it can handle a much wider range of requests and conversations. Putting it inside Gemini Tasks turns phoning into one more tool an agent can call, next to browsing and app control. The 1 trillion figure counts how often business details collected by calls appeared in Google products, not the number of calls.
stories.industry: Most small businesses can only be reached by phone or a basic website, so voice agents are how general assistants finish real-world errands. It also raises consent and disclosure questions for the people receiving the calls.
stories.you: If you run a service with a phone line, expect AI callers and plan how to handle them (clear menus, structured booking options). If you build agents, voice is now a realistic tool channel, with latency as the main engineering constraint.
terms: Duplex
Google's AI system that holds natural phone conversations to complete tasks like bookings.
Foundation model
A large general model trained on broad data and adapted to many tasks.
stories.why: Google published the details on its Research blog this week.
stories.source: Google Research blog (via Rio Rundown) · 21 Nov

stories.title: Nvidia reportedly near deal for diffusion-LLM maker Inception
stories.plain: Nvidia is reported to be nearing an acquisition of Inception, a startup whose Mercury models generate text by refining many tokens at once instead of one by one. Inception has told customers its Mercury API will shut down on 28 December.
stories.eng: Mercury uses diffusion: it drafts a block of tokens and refines them over several passes, with a transformer doing the revisions, instead of standard autoregressive next-token decoding. Inception reports Mercury 3 at 1,068 tokens per second on Nvidia GPUs. Nvidia's own Nemotron-Labs Diffusion work includes a mode where diffusion drafts tokens and an autoregressive model verifies them.
specs: More than 40x the parameters of Mercury 1
stories.point: The point: the main GPU vendor may be buying the leading alternative to token-by-token text generation.
stories.means: Today's chat models write one token at a time, so speed is capped by how fast a GPU can run one forward pass after another. Diffusion language models, borrowed from image generation, produce many tokens in parallel and clean them up over a few steps, which can be much faster for the same quality. The deal is reported, not announced, and Inception's wind-down notice does not give a reason for closing the API.
stories.industry: Inference cost and latency now matter more than raw training scale, especially for agents that make many calls. If Nvidia owns a fast decoding method, it can tune it to its hardware and offer it to every customer, which puts pressure on rivals selling speed.
stories.you: If you use the Mercury API, export your data and migrate before 28 December. More broadly, diffusion or draft-and-verify decoding may show up in your serving stack as a speed option; check how it handles your output constraints.
terms: Autoregressive
Generating text one token at a time, each based on all previous tokens.
Diffusion LLM
A model that drafts many tokens at once and refines them over several passes.
stories.why: Earlier reports said Inception had talks with Microsoft and interest from SpaceX at an asking price above $1 billion.
stories.source: The Neuron (citing The Information) · 20 Nov; Inception wind-down notice

stories.title: Harvard-led team gets $12M to have AI design quantum error correction
stories.plain: The US Department of Energy gave a Harvard-led team $12 million to use AI to design quantum error correction tailored to specific scientific problems. Partners include MIT, three national labs, QuEra, NVIDIA and Anthropic.
stories.eng: The project trains models to learn which errors matter for workloads in quantum simulation, materials, chemistry and nuclear science, then uses AI to design codes and decoders for them and tests them on neutral-atom hardware at Harvard, MIT and QuEra. It builds on an April preprint with a neural-network decoder and on work with QuEra and Anthropic using LLMs to find better quantum circuits.
specs: $12M, DOE (one of 12 Phase II Genesis Mission awards)
Up to 17x lower error rate, thousands of times faster
MIT, Cornell, Los Alamos, Berkeley Lab, Sandia, QuEra, NVIDIA, Anthropic
stories.point: The point: government money is now backing AI as the designer of quantum error correction, not just a helper.
stories.means: Qubits are noisy, so useful quantum computers need error correction: spreading one reliable 'logical' qubit across many physical ones and constantly decoding errors. Generic codes waste qubits protecting against errors that do not matter for a given calculation. This project lets AI tailor codes and decoders to each application, which could cut how many qubits are needed. On the same day, QuEra and UC collaborators described Qubrio, a multi-agent LLM compiler for neutral-atom machines.
stories.industry: Frontier AI labs are entering quantum through software: Anthropic and NVIDIA are named partners. If AI shortens the path to fault tolerance, timelines for useful chemistry and materials simulation move closer.
stories.you: Quantum error correction is becoming an ML problem with clear inputs, outputs and simulators, the kind of search task LLM agents are good at. If you work on optimisation or compilers, this is an area where those skills transfer.
terms: Quantum error correction
Encoding one logical qubit across many physical qubits so errors can be detected and fixed.
Decoder
The classical algorithm that reads error signals and decides which correction to apply.
stories.why: Lukin compared quantum computers to a new kind of telescope for science.
stories.source: Harvard Gazette · 20 Nov; Quantum Computing Report · 20 Nov

stories.title: Kaiser models flag pregnancy risks from routine records by week 12
stories.plain: Kaiser Permanente and MIT researchers trained AI models on ordinary electronic health records to predict seven pregnancy complications. Gestational diabetes, gestational hypertension and preeclampsia could be flagged as early as 12 weeks.
stories.eng: The team built 49 models, one per complication at each of seven timepoints spaced six weeks apart, trained on 80% of records and tested on 20%. An external test on NIH's All of Us data showed lower performance, which improved after adapting the models with All of Us data. The study is in Communications Health.
stories.point: The point: routine data clinics already collect can spot some pregnancy risks months earlier, but models do not travel well between health systems.
stories.means: Complications like preeclampsia are often found late, when options are fewer. These models use only data entered in normal care, so no new tests are needed. Outcomes at birth, such as preterm birth and stillbirth, were harder to predict even at 24 weeks. The drop on outside data is a standard problem: a model learns the habits of one hospital system, and the researchers stress that it is not yet shown that earlier flags improve outcomes.
stories.industry: Health AI is moving from imaging into prediction from records, where data is plentiful. The study's external validation and adaptation step is the kind of evidence regulators and hospitals increasingly ask for before deployment.
stories.you: If you build models on data from one organisation, test them on a second source before claiming accuracy; expect a drop and plan for fine-tuning. Time-sliced models, one per point in a process, are a simple pattern for early warning.
terms: EHR
Electronic health record: the digital chart of diagnoses, labs, medications and visits.
External validation
Testing a model on data from a different source than it was trained on.
stories.why: Next steps include adding ultrasound, clinical notes and biomarkers.
stories.source: Kaiser Permanente Division of Research · 19 Nov

stories.title: US and China agree humans must oversee military AI, says Bessent
stories.plain: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Donald Trump and Xi Jinping agreed in Shenzhen that humans must oversee military decisions involving advanced AI. At the same time, the US further restricted Chinese access to advanced chips and remote computing.
stories.eng: A Commerce Department rule now requires licences for advanced AI chip shipments to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, closing routes through overseas data centres. Separately, House records showed approvals for 879,868 Nvidia H200 and AMD MI325X chips for Chinese firms as of 11 May.
stories.point: The point: Washington and Beijing found narrow common ground on military AI while the US keeps tightening the compute squeeze.
stories.means: Keeping a human responsible for lethal decisions is the most widely shared principle in AI arms-control talks, so a US–China statement on it matters even if details are thin. The chip rule targets a loophole: Chinese firms renting high-end GPUs in Southeast Asian data centres. Moonshot AI reportedly dropped a $150 million Indonesia deal after the rule. Nvidia says it has stopped shipping H200s to China despite holding some licences.
stories.industry: Compute access is now foreign policy. Cloud providers in the affected countries face new compliance work, and Chinese labs are pushed further toward domestic chips. At APEC, Trump also said the US would not accept international regulation of superintelligence.
stories.you: If you deploy GPUs or sell compute in Southeast Asia or Brazil, check customer screening and licence requirements. If you depend on Chinese open-weight models, watch how compute limits affect their release pace.
terms: Export licence
Government permission required to ship controlled technology to certain countries or buyers.
Human oversight
A rule that a person, not an AI system, makes or approves a decision.
stories.why: Bessent spoke on Friday after the Trump–Xi meeting held alongside APEC in Shenzhen.
stories.source: Reuters (via Rio Rundown) · 21 Nov; Technology Org · 19 Nov; The Neuron · 20 Nov

stories.title: UN opens Bridgetown AI safety summit as Trump rejects global rules
stories.plain: UN Secretary-General António Guterres and Barbados Prime Minister Mia Mottley are co-hosting a special AI safety summit in Bridgetown that opens on Monday. It aims to help countries build their own capacity to respond to AI risks.
stories.eng: UN envoy Amandeep Singh Gill described the proposed framework as a tool for nations to build safety infrastructure, such as incident response teams. The gap is large: high-income countries have 500 such teams, low-income countries six.
specs: 500 in high-income vs 6 in low-income countries
Signed by 32 states and the European Commission
stories.point: The point: global AI safety talks are shifting toward basic response capacity for poorer countries, just as the US rejects international rules.
stories.means: Most AI safety work happens in a few rich countries and labs, while harms like deepfakes, fraud and AI-assisted cyberattacks hit everywhere. Incident response teams detect and handle such events; without them, a country cannot even see the problem. The Bridgetown framework is voluntary and focuses on building that capacity. The same week, Trump said at APEC that the US would not let global initiatives stifle the technology.
stories.industry: AI governance is fragmenting: the EU regulates, the US prefers national control and export rules, and the UN pushes capacity building. Companies operating globally face a patchwork rather than one standard.
stories.you: If your product runs in many countries, expect different incident-reporting expectations by region. Keeping good logs and a clear incident process for AI failures will satisfy most of them.
terms: Incident response team
A group that detects, investigates and coordinates response to security or AI-related incidents.
Frontier model
The most capable AI models at a given time, usually from the largest labs.
stories.why: Seventeen states and ten AI developers endorsed a related call from a summit hosted by Emmanuel Macron.
stories.source: UN News (via Rio Rundown) · 21 Nov; Yahoo (via Rio Rundown) · 21 Nov

stories.title: Runway takes its video world models into robotics with Praxis-1
stories.plain: Runway, known for AI video tools, is extending its video and Praxis-1 world models to robotics. Its co-CEO says Praxis-1 leads the RoboLab leaderboard among open-weights robotics models.
stories.eng: A world model learns how scenes change over time from video, so it can predict what happens after an action; that prediction can train or plan for robots instead of costly real-world trials. Runway also acquired the Kinetix team as part of the push.
specs: 95% of the Fortune 100 use its tools
stories.point: The point: video-generation companies see robotics as the next market for the same world models.
stories.means: Robots learn slowly because real-world data is expensive to collect. A model that has watched huge amounts of video and can simulate what happens next gives robots a cheap practice ground. Runway, Google (Genie) and Nvidia are all pitching video world models this way. The leaderboard claim is Runway's own and limited to open-weights models.
stories.industry: Physical AI is attracting money because language models have used up most easy text data, while the physical world is largely untapped. Companies with strong video models have a head start on simulation for robots.
stories.you: If you work on robotics or simulation, open-weights world models are becoming a practical source of synthetic training data. Check how well their predictions hold up on your own hardware before relying on them.
terms: World model
An AI model that predicts how an environment will change, often from video.
Open weights
Model parameters released for anyone to download and run.
stories.why: Runway also launched a plug-in with OpenAI's ChatGPT.

stories.title: John Deere buys Orchard AI for plant-by-plant crop vision
stories.plain: John Deere acquired Orchard AI (Orchard Robotics), a startup that uses cameras and image analysis to monitor crops plant by plant. Financial terms were not disclosed.
stories.eng: Orchard's cameras mount on farm machinery and use computer vision to measure crops as vehicles pass, giving growers plant-level data on things like fruit counts and health. Deere plans to add this crop intelligence to its machines for specialty-crop growers.
stories.point: The point: the biggest farm machinery maker is buying perception, turning tractors into data-collecting robots.
stories.means: Specialty crops like fruit and nuts are labour-heavy and hard to measure: growers often estimate yields by sampling a few trees. Cameras that see every plant as machines drive past give exact counts and early warnings. Deere already sells autonomy and precision spraying; adding plant-level vision lets machines decide per plant. The deal follows a week of physical-AI deals, including Rockwell's agreement to buy mobile-robot maker AGILOX.
stories.industry: Physical AI money is flowing into industries with clear, measurable returns, such as farming, logistics and inspection, not only humanoids. Incumbent equipment makers are buying startups to own the data layer.
stories.you: Computer vision at the edge (on moving vehicles, with poor connectivity) is a growing engineering niche. If you work on vision, these settings reward robust models that run on modest hardware.
terms: Specialty crops
Fruits, nuts, vegetables and similar high-value crops, as opposed to grains.
Edge inference
Running AI models on the device itself rather than in the cloud.
stories.why: Deere announced the deal on Thursday.
stories.source: John Deere (via RobotToday) · 20 Nov; GeekWire (via Rio Rundown) · 21 Nov

concepts.name: Automated AI research
concepts.desc: Agents that do the engineering work of building and training AI systems themselves, from training code to serving and experiments.

OpenAI's Performance Factory: Codex agents ran 1,700+ investigations of ChatGPT slowdowns and found 600+ root causes in about three months.
19 Nov
OpenAI: its coding agents completed 46% of 2–4 hour internal research tasks in October, up from 23% in March; 4–8 hour tasks rose from 13% to 35%.
19 Nov
OpenAI's models cut a multiplier's area ~15% and improved AMD flagship GPU blocks by up to 14% in power, performance and area.
18 Nov
Meta's Ranking Engineer Agent automates over 60% of technique propagation across ads models, projecting over $45M in compute savings this year.
18 Nov
CMU's Singularity-Bench: Opus 5.5 in Claude Code matches or beats human-built references on all six AI-stack tasks (index 1.25; others ~0.6).

OpenAI rates GPT-6.2 Astra High for AI self-improvement, its first public model to reach it; it clears the MLE-Bench cutoff but not NanoGPT or PostTrainBench Lite.

Google Antigravity /teamwork: Gemini 4 agent teams with fresh-context handoffs and falsifiers formalise the Weil conjectures and port libgav1 to faster Rust.

Anthropic Fellows: a single coordinator beats per-user agent teams by ~10-45 points on shared-resource tasks; MAMUBench released.

concepts.name: Agents that prove code correct
concepts.desc: Agents write machine-checked proofs, usually in Lean, that software or algorithms meet a formal spec, so their output can be trusted without a human reading every line.

Levent Alpöge claims a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis found with Claude and released as a Lean formalization in 14 parts; not yet independently checked.

Physicist Nathaniel Craig says GPT-6 Astra led the proof in a candidate lattice definition of the Standard Model, shipped with a Lean 4 formalization.

Google's LEAP framework produces a ~1.8M-line machine-checked Lean formalisation of the Weil conjectures over 28,800+ subagent calls.

DeepMind's AlphaProof Code verifies Signal's one-to-one crypto down to machine instructions; humans review ~1% of the code.
9 Nov
~1,000 Claude agents formalize Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean in about 30 hours.
6 Nov
Google builds a Lean library where agents write quantum programs whose correctness and cost are proven.

concepts.name: Agent memory and continual learning
concepts.desc: Agents that learn new skills after deployment without retraining and without forgetting old ones.

Meta FAIR: agent-optimized memory prompts score 56.0 vs 44.6 for the best hand-written ones, and part of the gain is distilled into weights with a rank-64 LoRA.
19 Nov
Perplexity Brain wrote over 80,000 personal agent skills for over 20,000 users from experience, 1 Aug–14 Nov.
19 Nov
ARISE memory architecture for enterprise agents gains 10.9 points on SOP-Bench (arXiv 2611.23588).
18 Nov
Microsoft's Copilot Autopilot ships in early access as an always-on agent with its own Entra identity and memory.

Stanford open-sources Memorilla: a 194M module compresses a document store into 16 soft tokens for a frozen Qwen3-8B, beating full context on FactKG with 108x fewer tokens.
9 Nov
MIRIX-2.0: six typed memory agents plus a provenance hypergraph and offline AutoDream consolidation reach 91.4% on LoCoMo and lead LongMemEval-S by 14.3 points.

concepts.name: Continual world models
concepts.desc: Models that learn physics and causality from observation and keep updating after training. The bridge from text to physical tasks.
signals: 21 Nov
Runway extends its Praxis-1 world model to robotics, claiming the top open-weights spot on the RoboLab leaderboard.

Genie 4 opens to Google AI Ultra subscribers and, a day later, the Gemini API: 720p, up to 24 fps, sessions up to about two minutes.

Google opens Genie 4 interactive world model to eligible AI Ultra subscribers.

AMD closes ~$8.2B World Labs acquisition; Fei-Fei Li becomes EVP and chief scientist.

NeurIPS 2026 runs a dedicated Continual World Models workshop, with papers on test-time adaptation and multi-agent world models.

NTT physics-constrained video world model lifts robot shelf-loading success from 73.1% to 92.3%; airport baggage trials planned with Mujin.

concepts.name: AI-discovered quantum algorithms
concepts.desc: Using LLM search to cut the gate and qubit cost of quantum algorithms, moving the date quantum becomes useful.
signals: 20 Nov
DOE gives a Harvard-led team (with QuEra, NVIDIA, Anthropic) $12M to have AI design application-specific error-correction codes and decoders.
19 Nov
AI now designs quantum error correction: IBM's LLM-guided OpenEvolve found 465 code candidates; QC Design reports a 14.6x median lower logical error rate.

QuEra, Harvard and Anthropic publicise AI-designed circuits with up to 9,100× lower space-time cost.

Google preprint: agents writing Lean-verified quantum programs beat baselines by up to 290x on arithmetic and 11x on fusion-relevant simulation.

Preprint: modular inversion circuit with 17× fewer gates after a 53-hour run.

concepts.name: Instruction–data separation
concepts.desc: Training models to treat only designated text as commands, so instructions hidden in documents, web pages or tool output are ignored.

Reuters: Meta's Muse agent read Signal messages via Android notification and macOS accessibility permissions; Apple added agent-specific prompts.

Citi, PNC and Citizens join JPMorgan and BofA in making customers liable for third-party agent actions, even if the agent is hacked.

IQM and Pasqal back NVIDIA's Slurm 26.11 HRES work at SC26, making QPUs a schedulable shared resource next to GPUs; IQM already runs at ORNL, VTT, LRZ and CINECA.

Q-CTRL raises US$290M, led by Salesforce Ventures with AMD Ventures joining, to scale AI-driven quantum control software.

AMD plans an equity stake in PsiQuantum and the two tune an ML decoder, PRISM, for real-time error correction on accelerators.

Cleveland Clinic, RIKEN and IBM pass 12,000 atoms in quantum-classical drug binding simulation.

concepts.desc: Robots moving from demos into shops, pharmacies, warehouses and public markets.

eras.name: Large language models
eras.short: Models trained to predict the next word turn out to write, translate and code.
eras.how: A transformer is trained on a large share of the public internet to predict the next token. Capabilities appear with scale: GPT-3 could do tasks it was never trained for, given a few examples in the prompt.
eras.built: Autocomplete, text generation APIs, early GitHub Copilot.
eras.broke: Raw models ramble, make things up and do not follow instructions reliably.

eras.name: Chatbots
eras.short: Instruction tuning and human feedback make models useful in a conversation.
eras.how: Fine-tune the base model on examples of good answers, then use reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) so it prefers helpful, safe replies.
eras.built: Chat interfaces, customer support bots, writing assistants.
eras.broke: The model only knows its training data and cannot look anything up or do anything.

eras.name: RAG and tool use
eras.short: Models get access to your documents and to APIs.
eras.how: Retrieval-augmented generation fetches relevant documents and pastes them into the prompt. Function calling lets the model output a structured call to an API you define.
eras.broke: One question, one answer. Multi-step tasks still needed a human driving every step.

eras.name: Workflows
eras.short: Engineers chain model calls into fixed pipelines.
eras.how: You write the steps in code: classify, then retrieve, then draft, then check. The model fills in each step, but the control flow is yours.
eras.built: Document processing pipelines, LangChain-style chains, eval harnesses.
eras.broke: Fixed pipelines break on anything you did not anticipate. Real tasks need the system to decide what to do next.

eras.name: Agents
eras.short: The model decides the next step itself, in a loop with tools.
eras.how: A loop: the model looks at the goal and results so far, picks a tool, runs it, reads the output, repeats until done. Reasoning models that think before answering made these loops far more reliable.
eras.built: Coding agents, computer-use agents, MCP servers that expose tools to any agent.
eras.broke: Agents worked for minutes, then drifted, looped or lost track on long tasks.

eras.name: Autonomous agents
eras.short: Agents run for hours on real work in sandboxes, with little supervision.
eras.how: Better long-horizon training, sandboxed environments, checkpoints and the ability to run tests let an agent own a whole task: open the repo, make the change, run CI, open a pull request.
eras.built: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity; agents opening PRs while you sleep.
eras.broke: One agent is one thread of work. Large problems need many in parallel.

eras.name: Multi-agent orchestration
eras.short: A planner agent splits work across specialist agents.
eras.how: An orchestrator breaks a goal into subtasks, hands them to worker agents with different tools or prompts, and merges the results.
eras.built: Agent teams for research, code migration and analysis; orchestration frameworks.
eras.broke: Coordination overhead grows fast, and someone still has to check every worker’s output.

eras.name: Agent swarms with verifiers
eras.short: Hundreds to thousands of agents work against an automatic checker that accepts only correct results.
eras.how: Instead of trusting agents, you trust the verifier: a proof checker, test suite or simulator. Agents propose, the verifier filters, survivors get refined. Memory layers start letting agents keep what they learn.
eras.built: 1,000-agent formal proof of Fermat in ~30h; AI-designed quantum circuits beating human designs; Signal's crypto code verified by agents in Lean.
eras.broke: Still open: it only works where a strict automatic check exists.
eras.marks: Fermat formalization (9 Nov 2026), AI quantum circuits (10 Nov 2026), AlphaProof Code on Signal (10 Nov 2026)

eras.name: World models and continual learning
eras.short: Contenders for what comes next: models that learn physics from observation and keep learning after deployment.
eras.how: World models simulate how an environment will change when you act, which lets agents plan in the physical world. Continual learning updates the model from experience without retraining from scratch.
eras.built: Research prototypes, robotics simulation, NeurIPS 2026 workshops.
eras.broke: Not yet reliable outside labs. Watch Frontier for signals.
eras.marks: Genie, V-JEPA, Continual World Models workshop (NeurIPS 2026)
